item.title: Transparent When You Want It, Private When You Need It
item.description: Public blockchains solved settlement. They didn't solve privacy. Institutions need to protect positions, counterparty relationships, and transaction amounts without abandoning transparency entirely - and every architecture that tried to solve this hit the same wall. Protocol-level privacy locks everything. Permissioned chains recreate centralization. Separate privacy layers fragment liquidity. Stellar's answer is different. Cryptographic primitives baked into the base layer, two production-ready privacy models on top, and the institution decides what to reveal and to whom. Transparent when you want it. Private when you need it.

item.title: Why Privacy Matters More Than Ever in 2026
item.description: Privacy is no longer a cypherpunk slogan - it’s turning into core blockchain infrastructure. Public blockchains proved they can move money quickly, but they also expose balances, relationships, and behavior permanently. The next wave of networks isn’t competing on speed or fees, but on who can protect financial data without hiding everything.

item.title: Social Recovery Wallets are Broken by Design
item.description: Social recovery sounds like a friendly safety net — until it isn't. In reality, it hands your security over to the very humans crypto was built to eliminate from the trust model. A UX-driven mirage of safety masks the vulnerabilities of guardianship, turning recovery into the ultimate attack vector.

item.title: The Fake Treasury Playbook - How Protocols Inflate Their War Chests
item.description: Behind flashy treasury dashboards lie recycled tokens, illiquid assets, and deceptive accounting — in Web3, war chests are often just smoke and mirrors crafted to inspire trust, not to fund survival.

item.title: DeFi’s UX Problem Is a Feature, Not a Bug
item.description: DeFi’s chaotic interfaces aren’t a bug — they’re a feature. Confusion keeps users compliant, disoriented, and easier to exploit in a space where clarity threatens profit and understanding kills the hype.
